Commercial breaks as taken from an episode of the Price is Right on RKO General-owned CBS affiliate WNAC in Boston.

WNAC, as presented here, no longer exists. The station was forced off the air on May 22, 1982 due to RKO General's corporate misconduct and accounting fraud. A new station, WNEV, signed on the next morning under a new license, assuming the CBS affiliation from WNAC, as well as its studio facility, transmitter, programming, and most of the staff. recentItems.title: September 22, 1995 Commercial Breaks–WTTE (Fox, Columbus)
recentItems.description:
Channel 37 is a proud partner of BROADCAST PLAZA, Discord's media discussion community — Join us! https://discord.gg/D8m5Thxpcp

Commercial breaks taken from episodes of "Strange Luck", "the X-Files" and "Star Trek Voyager" on Sinclair-owned Fox (and secondary UPN) affiliate WTTE in Columbus, Ohio.

The next year, Sinclair bought River City Broadcasting, which owned ABC affiliate WSYX in the market. WTTE was then passed off to Glencairn, a company closely related to Sinclair and which would later become Cunningham Broadcasting—though Sinclair continued to operate WTTE through various service agreements. In 2021, as part of the introduction of ATSC 3.0 in the Columbus market, Sinclair moved WTTE's Fox programming and IP to WSYX 6.3, leaving WTTE to run the company's low-rent TBD feed, which is normally relegated to the subchannels of fellow Sinclair-owned/operated stations, on 28.1.
